a combination of the two drugs, camptothecins and AG1478, was synergistic and altered the protein profile in EKVX cells.
we have shown that the combination of the two drugs, AG1478 and camptothecins, is more effective than either drug alone.

the combination of the EGFR inhibitor AG1478 and the topoisomerase I inhibitor CPT,10-H, is synergistic against EKVX cells and that a proteomic profile of the ECVX cell line was altered by treatment with these drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a pharmacoproteomics approach to study the synergistic effects of two anticancer drugs.

the identification and quantitation of protein expression in cancer cells treated with chemotherapeutic agents using a pharmacoproteomic approach, which may provide a better understanding of the mechanisms of action of chemotherapeutic agents.
identifying the proteins whose expression is altered in response to chemotherapeutic agents, with a particular emphasis on synergistic combinations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has demonstrated the feasibility of the use of capillary-LC-MS/MS to identify proteins that are differentially expressed between treated and untreated cells, and that these changes can be correlated to the observed biological response.

the synergistic action observed between AG1478 and 10-OH was due to the combination of the effects of each drug alone, as well as the effect of the drug combination, and that this synergistic effect was reflected in altered expression levels of multiple proteins.
the synergistic action between the EGFR inhibitor and the topoisomerase I inhibitor was reflected in the proteome of the EKVx cell line, as shown in this study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of two agents that act on different targets, in this case the EGFR and topoisomerase I, can lead to synergistic cytotoxic effects.
a pharmacoproteomics approach using capillary-LCMS/MS can be used for the evaluation of chemotherapeutic agents.
we have shown a pharmacoproteomics analysis of a cell line treated with a chemotherapeutic drug and an EGFR inhibitor.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proteomic analysis of a cancer cell line treated with a combination of chemotherapeutic agents is a viable approach to study the mechanism of action of these agents and their combinations and can provide a basis to develop new drug combinations.
the proteomic approach can be used to identify the mechanism of action of drugs, and that the combination of AG1479 and CPT, 10-O-H is an effective treatment for the cell line EKVx.
